The clips play BACK TO BACK as a medley, with no narration between them (verbatim, in play order; the channels were not

CLIP 2 id=feb4b72f301cde9d380d | show: Natalie Brunell | speaker NOT verified (credit the show only) | 9.6 s | "And that's not to say that it's bad. It's that self -custody Bitcoin's a responsibility. If I have a gun, it's a responsibility. Sovereignty is a responsibility."

ONE JOIN NEEDS HELP: a blind viewer who watched these clips back to back could not follow the jump from
CLIP 01 to CLIP 02 ("unclear referent for 'that's not to say it's bad'; abrupt shift to responsibility"). Write ONE "bridge", heard between them: as short as it can be (at most 12 words); it only makes
the next clip's subject or referent clear (its show and its topic, or a question); it never says what the next speaker
thinks. Give "why": one sentence on why a viewer could not follow the jump without it. If you judge a viewer CAN
follow this jump without narration, give "bridge": null (these clips then do not sit together, and other clips are
picked).
Write:
- "takeaway": 17-20 words in short declarative sentences: the point the medley adds up to, as YOUR OWN
  commentary (your opinion or conclusion), a point and not a summary, never a restatement of any clip.
  The takeaway may characterise what the clips SAID, never what WILL happen. Two kinds were refused: a forecast or a permanence claim stated as fact ('Bitcoin outlasts politics.'), and a superlative that upgrades a speaker's hedged view to a settled claim ("Bitcoin's apolitical design is the real productivity story." after a speaker's 'I think Bitcoin will outperform').
- "title": ONE title, at most 70 characters; "caption": ONE caption, at most 220 characters. Both carry the angle.
Every line gives "cites": the ids of the clips it relies on (none for your own commentary).
RULES (a line that breaks one is rejected):
- NEVER restate a clip's claim, and never repeat its words: the clip says it, in its own words.
- Your OWN commentary is an opinion or a conclusion, nothing else: no checkable fact, number, price, date, named person
  or company; never what a speaker thinks or how speakers relate; no prediction of what will happen; no advice or
  instruction to the viewer (no "you should", "your job", "must"); no accusation; nothing that sounds like a quote.
- Say what a speaker says or thinks ONLY for a clip marked VERIFIED, by that name, with the clip's own hedge: "thinks"
  for "I think", "feels" for "I feel like", "says" only for a flat statement. For any other clip credit the SHOW only
  ("on Coin Bureau", "from What Bitcoin Did's show"), never "<name> says" or "<name> discusses".
- Never say or imply that channels agree, answer, rebut or react to each other.
- No price level; no advice to buy, sell or use leverage; no quotes except a clip's exact words; no "destroys",
  "slams", "exposes", "admits", "confirms", "caught".
- A line that names a show, a person or Bitcoin's price cites the clips it comes from.
- Never give anyone a ROLE the clips' own words do not state: no "guest", "host", "co-host", "analyst", "expert",
  "economist", "strategist", "interviewer", "presenter", "anchor", "panelist" or "commentator". A role is a claim
  (law L-v): say "he", "she" or "the speaker", or credit the show.
HOUSE STYLE (PBX's standing copy rules; a line that breaks one is rejected):
- Everywhere: no hashtags; no em-dash or en-dash (use a period or a comma); no emoji; no hedging words (may, might, could be, perhaps, possibly, arguably); no AI-sounding phrasing (it's worth noting, it is worth noting, delve, delves, delving, tapestry, testament to, in today's world, ever-evolving, game-changer, navigate the).
- CAPTION: all lowercase, names too; one or two short sentences, at most 24 words in all; never talk about the video itself (this medley, this video, this clip, these clips, builds toward, this montage); no money words (opportunity, invest, profit, get rich, to the moon, buy the dip, financial advice).
- TITLE: at most 8 words, plain; never open with a possessive (not "Bitcoin's overlooked value comes from ..." but "The market no government owns").
- TAKEAWAY: at most 20 words in short declarative sentences: a point, not a summary; never open with "what stands out", "it's worth noting", "ultimately", "in the end"; no "which makes ..." clause.
- PBX MAX's voice, for its rhythm, never its words: "No ruler. Just rules nobody gets to bend. That's the idea, and it's the part most people still miss when they look at Bitcoin."
